S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.

subtypes.Future Hopelessness: The persistent conviction that the future holds no possibility of improvement.
subtypes.Belief in Impossibility of Improvement: The belief that the current situation will absolutely not get better.
subtypes.Helpless Resignation: A state of helplessness and resignation, believing that nothing will change despite effort.
subtypes.Chronic Pessimism: A persistent tendency to view everything negatively and fail to consider positive possibilities.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (PDD), or dysthymia, is a chronic mood disorder characterized by a depressed mood lasting at least two years in adults, accompanied by additional depressive features and clinically significant distress or impairment. Compared with major depressive disorder, PDD tends to have a more insidious onset, a longer and more stable course, and symptoms that are less severe but more enduring, often becoming embedded in a person's sense of self. Patients frequently present with long‑standing low mood, low energy, and pessimism that they may describe as their "normal" way of being, leading to underrecognition and delayed treatment. Comorbidity with major depressive episodes (double depression), anxiety disorders, and medical conditions is common, and functional impairment can be substantial despite relatively mild to moderate symptom intensity at any given time.

patient.personality: Gustavo is a talkative, competitive, and culturally engaged storyteller who prides himself on disciplined project management and bringing people together around art, history, and good food.
patient.stressor: About three and a half years ago, Gustavo underwent an unexpected cardiac procedure after a routine hiking trip left him unusually winded, which forced him to abruptly scale back his consulting work, tours, and mountain hikes. Accustomed to being the energetic center of construction sites, museum groups, and dinner parties, he struggled with the slow pace of cardiac rehabilitation and the new limitations imposed by his doctors, feeling increasingly sidelined from the community projects that had defined his identity. Over the following years, as he turned down mural initiatives and historic‑building tours due to low stamina, he became progressively more withdrawn from the philosophy club, community theater, and social cooking he once organized, noticing that each attempt to resume his usual rhythm left him feeling more depleted and less motivated. When his reduced activity began to affect his ability to reliably manage even small consulting contracts and he found himself canceling social commitments because he "just didn't have it in him anymore," his primary care physician, concerned about the chronic decline in his functioning, referred him for a psychiatric evaluation.
patient.chief_complaint: “I feel exhausted all the time, no matter how much I rest, and I just don’t have the energy to do the things I used to.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: Ever since the heart scare, it’s like someone turned the dimmer switch down on my mood and left it there—I go through the motions at home, but most days I feel this dull, gray heaviness in my chest, even when I’m sitting in a sunny plaza or listening to music I used to love.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: What wears me down is that from the moment I get out of bed I already feel as if I’ve put in a full day on a construction site, so even small things like sorting paperwork for a tiny consulting job or walking around the block leave me wiped out and needing to lie down.

S083.name: Hopelessness
S083.description: A feeling of despair or having no hope for the future.
S083.manifestation: I catch myself thinking, more often than I like to admit, that this is just the long, slow fade-out and that no amount of rehab, diet, or positive thinking is really going to bring back the man who used to lead hikes and theater projects, so I don’t see much to look forward to beyond just marking time.
